name: Freebuff
vendor: Codebuff Inc. (CodebuffAI); ad-funded free product built on Codebuff

surfaces.label: Freebuff CLI (npm `freebuff`, bin `freebuff`). The npm bin is only a Node launcher (`node .../bin/freebuff`, argv[0] is `node`). It downloads a Bun-compiled Mach-O binary to ~/.config/manicode/freebuff and spawns it with argv[0] = that full path and the user's own args, so the process to match is the binary, never the launcher. The launcher stays alive as its parent. The same binary re-executes itself as `<same path> --terminal-command-broker` (detached, direct child) for every shell tool call; that helper is excluded here and is the working signal instead. `freebuff login` is a subcommand and is excluded.

Freebuff Desktop (Electron, bundle id com.freebuff.desktop). Matched on the local orchestrator that Freebuff.app starts as `<Freebuff.app>/Contents/Resources/bun/bun <Freebuff.app>/Contents/Resources/orchestrator/orchestrator.js` (argv is exactly those two entries; the runtime is `Resources/bun/bun`, or the sibling `Resources/bun/bun-baseline` on CPUs without AVX2, which the same path prefix also matches). The second args_contain entry is a specificity tie-break: the probe scores it +1, so this row beats the identical Freebuff Desktop surface still in codebuff.json. One orchestrator per app hosts every thread of every open project. NOT matched on the Electron main process (Contents/MacOS/Freebuff, capital F) or its Helper processes. Threads can use the Claude Code and Codex harnesses, so the orchestrator has claude and codex children that match those rows: drop them by ancestry.
Freebuff Web, Cloud and Chat (hosted at freebuff.com, no local process)

working_signals.name: freebuff
working_signals.meaning: Freebuff CLI only, only while a shell tool call runs: the binary re-executes itself (`<same path> --terminal-command-broker`, detached) as a DIRECT child and that helper runs `bash -c <cmd>` under it. Absent while the model streams or files are edited, and absent in a sponsored (ads) run, which uses a sandbox broker. Do not apply the generic rule 'ignore a child with the same executable as its parent' to this row. Counts only as a direct child.

working_signals.name: bash
working_signals.meaning: Freebuff Desktop orchestrator: shell tool calls run with no broker, so `bash -c <cmd>` is a direct child of the bun process while the command runs. Also true for a CLI sponsored run [inferred]. Weak, with known false positives on Desktop: the embedded terminal panel keeps the user's login shell (`$SHELL -l`) as a direct child for as long as the panel is open, so SHELL=/bin/bash reads as permanently working (zsh does not match this name); a project startup script runs as `bash -lc` for up to 120 s at thread setup. The schema has no argument filter for child_process. The exact Desktop answer is threads.turn_state = 'running' with a fresh turn_alive_at in <project>/.freebuff/desktop-v2.db, which the schema cannot express as a signal kind yet.

Freebuff CLI: while a run is live the SDK calls onStateSnapshot every 5 s, but a tick is skipped unless the run's messageHistory array was replaced since the last tick (a step boundary), then the CLI rewrites run-state.json and chat-messages.json (and chat-meta.json) in the chat directory; a synchronous save happens at turn end. So it is quiet during one long model call or one long tool call: it may raise working, its absence proves nothing. A process maps to a chat directory only through `--continue <id>`, otherwise by cwd basename plus newest mtime, which is a guess (and /new and /history change the directory). Desktop writes no such files.

Fallback and an unmeasured guess: nothing was running on this Mac. The CLI is a Bun OpenTUI renderer that also polls for ads and session admission; its idle CPU is unknown. On Desktop the tree includes claude and codex children.

waiting_signals.meaning: CLI: no hook, notification command, bell, OSC progress or power assertion, and no shell-command approval prompt was found in cli/src. Blocked-on-human states are TUI-only: the ask_user form (askUserState), the .agents trust prompt (`--trust-agents` skips it), login, and the free-tier waiting-room queue and session hours, which are not a turn. The terminal title is set to the typed input, not a state.

Freebuff Desktop only, weak: raised for `failed`, `stopped`, `merge-conflict` and `auto-stopped` (the only four values written in 0.0.154). These mean look at me, not a question or permission request. Pending questions (pendingQuestions) and sudo elevation requests (pendingElevations) are in-memory maps in the orchestrator, not in the schema [inferred from source: no column or table holds them]. Claude Code threads run with permissionMode bypassPermissions, so they raise no approval prompts.

hooks.config: None. Neither the Freebuff CLI nor Desktop reads a user hooks config. `run_file_change_hooks` is a tool the agent calls (a no-op in the SDK), not a lifecycle hook. Desktop uses Claude Code hooks internally for its own Claude threads (an elevation guard, claude-elevation-hook.js) and exposes nothing to the user. Nearest equivalents: custom agents in .agents/ and mcp.json in the repo (CLI, gated by a trust prompt), and per-thread state in .freebuff/desktop-v2.db (Desktop).
hooks.docs: none found; https://www.codebuff.com/docs and https://freebuff.com/desktop carry no hooks page

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry exporter in the public source or the shipped CLI binary. Product analytics go to PostHog and logs to an Axiom sink through the Freebuff API. The Desktop orchestrator bundle contains @opentelemetry/api and OTEL_* names only because it bundles the Claude Agent SDK; nothing configures an exporter for Freebuff itself.

notes: Freebuff is the free, ad-funded face of Codebuff; the codebuff row already carries Freebuff surfaces, and this row is the dedicated one. codebuff.json still lists the same Freebuff CLI and Desktop surfaces. Desktop: this row now scores 43 against 42 (second args_contain entry), so it wins. CLI: both rows score 27 (the path is as long as a generic path_contains can be, and the CLI has no mandatory argument), so probe.py keeps the row sorted first, codebuff.json, and Freebuff CLI processes report as Codebuff; `freebuff login` and `--version` also match there because codebuff.json has no exclude_args for them. Fix on the owner's side: drop the Freebuff surfaces from codebuff.json. CLI: the process to watch is the Bun binary ~/.config/manicode/freebuff, never the npm launcher (argv[0] is `node`). It shares ~/.config/manicode and the projects/*/chats store with Codebuff, so the store cannot say which binary wrote a chat; the process can. A CLI process holds one chat at a time but rotates it on /new and /history, and the store folder is the cwd basename, so map process to chat by `--continue <id>` when present and otherwise treat cwd plus newest mtime as a guess. Do not use tool_children: the permanent /bin/sh watchdog child would mark every idle CLI working. CLI working signals are weak by design (broker child during shell calls only; chat files rewritten about every 5 s at step boundaries; nothing during one long model call). Desktop: one orchestrator hosts every thread, so the exact per-thread answer is threads.turn_state = 'running' AND turn_alive_at within about 60 s (heartbeat is 30 s) in each open project's .freebuff/desktop-v2.db, reading those columns only and never messages. Find the databases with `lsof -p <orchestrator pid>` for open desktop-v2.db files [inferred: SQLite keeps the file open]. This needs a sqlite_row signal kind that the schema does not have, so the row falls back to the weak bash child. Desktop is not a host that can be ignored: its claude and codex children match the claude-code and codex rows and must be dropped by ancestry. Freebuff CLI also shows a waiting-room queue and session hours that are not a turn. Versions researched: npm freebuff 0.2.1 (2026-09-30), repo HEAD 41d91a7 (2026-09-30), Desktop 0.0.154 arm64, CLI binary darwin-arm64 0.2.1 (run for --version and --help only). Case: the Electron main executable is `Freebuff` with a capital F; the probe compares names case-sensitively, but a case-insensitive detector would match it against names ['freebuff'] and see Chromium helpers as tool children. Known limits, from the verification pass: session_id_args cannot tell a bare `--continue` from `--continue <id>`, so `freebuff --continue --trust-agents` yields `--trust-agents` as the id (the per_session path then does not exist, so transcript_write stays silent, harmless). The public repo HEAD moved to bc54be8 (2026-09-30T16:02Z) after the first pass; the files cited for the CLI are unchanged since 41d91a7.
